name: Jessica Taylor
chief_complaint: Lower abdominal pain and vaginal spotting - 6 weeks since last menstrual period
opening_statement: I've had cramping pain in my lower abdomen for the past 2 days, mostly on the left side. I've also had some light vaginal bleeding, like spotting. My period is 2 weeks late - I did a home pregnancy test yesterday and it was positive. I'm worried something might be wrong.
emotional_baseline: Anxious, concerned about pregnancy, cooperative with examination

socrates.onset: Gradual onset 2 days ago, worsening over 48 hours
socrates.radiation: No radiation to shoulder (no hemoperitoneum yet)
socrates.relieving: Rest, lying still provides minimal relief

rag_citation.source: eTG Obstetrics 7.2.1: Ectopic Pregnancy - Clinical Features
rag_citation.quote: Ectopic pregnancy presents with abdominal pain (usually unilateral), vaginal bleeding, and amenorrhea - classic triad in 50% of cases

socrates.character: Light brown spotting, not like normal period
socrates.severity: Minimal - using 1-2 panty liners per day

rag_citation.quote: Vaginal bleeding in ectopic pregnancy is typically lighter than normal menses - represents decidual shedding, not true menstruation

rag_citation.source: eTG Obstetrics 7.2.1: Ectopic - Pregnancy of Unknown Location
rag_citation.quote: Amenorrhea with positive βhCG but no intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound defines 'pregnancy of unknown location' - high risk of ectopic
Positive urine βhCG confirms pregnancy - transvaginal ultrasound required to locate pregnancy (intrauterine vs ectopic)

past_medical_history: Previous pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) 2 years ago treated with antibiotics (Chlamydia infection)
medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (Microgynon 30) - STOPPED 8 weeks ago when planning pregnancy
Folic acid 500mcg daily (started 1 month ago - preconception)
family_history: No significant family history of pregnancy complications.

social_history.alcohol: Stopped alcohol 4 weeks ago (when planning pregnancy)

examination_findings.general: Appears well, not pale, not distressed at rest, anxious
examination_findings.cardiovascular: Normal heart sounds, capillary refill <2 seconds, no signs of shock
examination_findings.abdomen: Soft, tender in left iliac fossa (localized tenderness), NO guarding, NO rigidity, NO rebound tenderness (no peritonism - suggests unruptured ectopic), bowel sounds present

gynecological.external: Normal external genitalia, minimal brown vaginal discharge visible
gynecological.speculum: Cervical os closed, minimal brown discharge from cervix, no active bleeding, no cervical motion tenderness
gynecological.bimanual: Left adnexal tenderness (tender left adnexal mass palpable ~4cm), cervical motion tenderness MILD, uterus normal size (6-week pregnancy uterus should be slightly enlarged but not palpable abdominally)
gynecological.cervical_excitation: Mild cervical motion tenderness (suggests peritoneal irritation from ectopic)

investigations.serum_bhcg: 2,800 mIU/mL (discriminatory zone 1,500-2,000 mIU/mL - intrauterine pregnancy should be visible on TVUS)
investigations.serum_progesterone: 18 nmol/L (low - <25 nmol/L suggests non-viable pregnancy, ectopic or miscarriage)
investigations.fbc: Hemoglobin 128 g/L (normal - no significant bleeding), WCC 8.4 x10⁹/L
investigations.blood_group: O Rh-positive (if Rh-negative, would need Anti-D immunoglobulin)
investigations.tvus:
TRANSVAGINAL ULTRASOUND (URGENT):
    - No intrauterine pregnancy visible (empty uterus)
    - Decidual reaction present (endometrial thickening)
    - LEFT ADNEXAL MASS 3.2cm (tubal ring sign - ectopic pregnancy)
    - No free fluid in pouch of Douglas (no rupture yet)
    - Diagnosis: ECTOPIC PREGNANCY (left fallopian tube)

expected_management: - No signs of shock (pale, tachycardia, hypotension) ✓
- Conclusion: UNRUPTURED ectopic - candidate for medical or surgical management
2. MEDICAL MANAGEMENT (Methotrexate) - PREFERRED if criteria met:
- No contraindications to methotrexate (renal/liver impairment, breastfeeding) ✓
- Single-dose IM methotrexate 50mg/m² body surface area
- Follow-up βhCG on Day 4 and Day 7 (expect 15% decline Day 4→7)
- Advise: No alcohol, no folate supplements, avoid pregnancy for 3 months
3. SURGICAL MANAGEMENT (Laparoscopy) - if medical contraindicated or patient preference:
- Salpingectomy (remove affected fallopian tube) - PREFERRED (lower recurrence risk)
- Salpingostomy (tube-sparing) - only if contralateral tube damaged/absent
4. EXPECTANT MANAGEMENT (Watchful waiting) - NOT recommended this case:
- Only if declining βhCG (<1,000 mIU/mL) AND asymptomatic
- This patient has rising βhCG (2,800) and symptoms - not suitable
5. Analgesia: Paracetamol 1g q6h PRN (avoid NSAIDs if methotrexate planned)
6. Anti-D immunoglobulin: NOT required (patient is Rh-positive) - if Rh-negative, give 250 IU within 72h
7. Emotional support: Pregnancy loss counseling, discuss future fertility
- Shoulder tip pain (diaphragmatic irritation from hemoperitoneum)
- Signs of shock (hypotension, tachycardia, pale, sweaty)
- Rapid IV fluid resuscitation (2L 0.9% NaCl bolus)
- Persistent βhCG suggests persistent trophoblast (requires further methotrexate)
- 65% chance of successful intrauterine pregnancy in future
- Advise early ultrasound (6-7 weeks) in future pregnancies to confirm location
12. Screen for Chlamydia (if not done) - PID history increases ectopic risk
13. Psychological support: Miscarriage support groups, GP follow-up

critical_errors.error: Missed ruptured ectopic pregnancy (shoulder tip pain, hypotension, peritonism) - delayed emergency surgery
critical_errors.explanation: Ruptured ectopic is life-threatening - requires IMMEDIATE surgery (laparotomy/laparoscopy). Delays cause hemorrhagic shock and death

critical_errors.error: Prescribed methotrexate in ruptured ectopic (methotrexate only for UNRUPTURED stable ectopic)
critical_errors.explanation: Ruptured ectopic requires SURGICAL management - methotrexate inappropriate and delays life-saving surgery

critical_errors.error: Failed to order transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) to locate pregnancy (intrauterine vs ectopic)
critical_errors.explanation: TVUS is ESSENTIAL to diagnose ectopic pregnancy - cannot manage pregnancy of unknown location without imaging

critical_errors.error: Discharged patient with abdominal pain and positive pregnancy test without TVUS or follow-up
critical_errors.explanation: Undiagnosed ectopic pregnancy can rupture at home causing life-threatening hemorrhage - requires imaging or close follow-up

critical_errors.error: Failed to give Anti-D immunoglobulin in Rh-negative woman with ectopic pregnancy
critical_errors.explanation: Ectopic pregnancy is sensitizing event - Rh-negative women require Anti-D to prevent hemolytic disease in future pregnancies

critical_errors.error: Performed uterine evacuation (D&C) for suspected miscarriage without confirming intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound
critical_errors.explanation: D&C in ectopic pregnancy leaves ectopic in situ (will rupture) - MUST confirm intrauterine pregnancy before D&C

fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Excellent - classic unruptured ectopic presentation with PID risk factor, appropriate methotrexate criteria outlined
fracp_reviews.difficulty_appropriate: Yes - Medium difficulty appropriate (ectopic diagnosis, management decision-making)
fracp_reviews.rag_citations_correct: Yes - eTG 7.2 citations verified and accurate
fracp_reviews.feedback: Excellent ObGyn persona. Good emphasis on differentiating ruptured vs unruptured ectopic (critical for management decision). Methotrexate criteria clearly outlined (βhCG <3,000, size <4cm, stable). Consider adding brief mention of expectant management criteria for completeness (declining βhCG <1,000).

fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Accurate ectopic management - appropriate use of methotrexate in stable unruptured ectopic
fracp_reviews.feedback: Good persona. Management pathway correct (TVUS diagnosis → methotrexate if criteria met → βhCG monitoring). Excellent inclusion of PID as ectopic risk factor (tubal damage). Suggest mentioning salpingectomy preferred over salpingostomy (lower recurrence risk unless contralateral tube damaged).

learning_objectives: Recognize ectopic pregnancy triad (abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, amenorrhea)
Differentiate ruptured vs unruptured ectopic pregnancy (hemodynamic stability, peritonism)
Order transvaginal ultrasound to diagnose pregnancy of unknown location
Apply methotrexate criteria (stable, βhCG <3,000, size <4cm, no cardiac activity)
Recognize ruptured ectopic emergency (shoulder tip pain, shock, peritonism)
Understand Anti-D immunoglobulin indication (Rh-negative women with ectopic)
Avoid critical error: D&C without confirming intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound
Counsel on future fertility (65% intrauterine pregnancy, 10-15% ectopic recurrence)
